CALL TO ORDER

Meeting called to order at 3:01 PM by Co-Chair Jamies Shuford.
Member Pam Chotiswatdi walks in at 3:04PM and Member Brandon Washington walks in at 3:05PM.

ROLL CALL

Commissioners Present: Tan, Wee, Shuford, Martins, Topolewski, Pezzelle, Washington,
Bambrick, Brezenoff, Wilson, Weithers, Boyce, Howat, Richert, Chotiswatdi

Also present: Stephanie Sosa, Community Program Specialist, Jennifer Santana, Secretary,
Alexa Dixson-Griggs, Community Program Specialist V, Paul Duncan, Attendee.

Roll call taken by Stephanie Sosa.

REGULAR AGENDA

1.  24-51716  Recommendation to receive and file all CoC Subcommittee Restructure.

  Alexa Dixson-Griggs, CoC Program Coordinator presented.
  • The CoC has 3 subcommittees; Policy & Standards, Coordinated Entry, and
  Quality, Data and Performance currently written into the charter and listed
  out in the bylaws.
  • The Policy and Standards Subcommittee is intended to review the charter
  annually and make recommendations to the Board. Currently this
  subcommittee is not performing its duties as assigned, which has required
  that HSB staff take on a more administrative role.
  • The Coordinated Entry Subcommittee is intended to include representation
  of all CoC agencies to that are co-located at a centralized access point of the
  MSC, to get together and discuss policy and procedures for the coordinated

  Page 1 of 6
   LONG BEACH CONTINUUM OF CARE MINUTES

  entry system, of which, a variation of that is occurring.
  • The Quality, Data, and Performance Subcommittee includes the HMIS and
  Agencies’ Administrators from each Long Beach CoC sub-recipient program.
  • Low attendance rates have made it difficult for items to move through the
  subcommittees and onto the larger Board docket in all three subcommittees.
  • The proposed restructuring would look to bring together services providers,
  HSB staff and those that work within the sphere of homeless services to
  have a dialogue on how to better the system at three key points of homeless
  services.
  • The new subcommittees would focus on access, matching & prioritization,
  and stability.
  • Board members had questions regarding the restructuring, specifically look
  at the access subcommittee.
  • City staff respond.

  A motion was made by Member Martins, seconded by Member Topolewski, to
  approve recommendation. The motion carried by the following vote:

  Yes:  14 Tan, Kennedy, Wee, Shuford, Martins, Pezzelle, Topolewski,
  Washington, Bambrick, Brezenoff, Boyce, Lee Lawler, Richert,
  Chotiswatdi
  No:  0 None
  Recused: 0 None
  Abstain: 1 Weithers
  Absent: 2 Wilson, Howat

2.  24-51717  Recommendation to receive and file the discussion on the CoC Board
  Participation.

  Alexa Dixson-Griggs, CoC Program Coordinator presented.
  • The Board has had difficulty meeting quorum at previous meetings and with
  some recent resignations, staff would like to remind the Board of what the
  CoC requirements are.
  • There are two seats open, and a few members are at risk of not meeting the
  board requirements.
  • Staff will be accepting nominations for the two vacancies via email.
  • Members had questions regarding attendance and a recommendation to
  reach out to DMH to have a seat on the Board.
  • Staff responded.

  A motion was made by Co-Chair Shuford, seconded by Member Boyce, to
  approve recommendation. The motion by the following vote:

  Yes:  13 Tan, Wee, Shuford, Martins, Pezzelle, Topolewski, Washington,

3.  24-51718  Recommendation to approve the Inactivity Policy.

  Alexa Dixson-Griggs, CoC Program Coordinator presented.
  • The inactive policy is a new policy that Long Beach CES hopes to adopt with
  approval from the Board as it can help ensure that clients can quickly be
  matched and connected to housing to avoid prolonged vacancies between
  tenants.
  • The adoption of the inactivity policy will help increase efficiency in the Long
  Beach Coordinated Entry System housing opportunity pool (HOP) referral
  process.
  • The policy stipulates that after 120 days of inactivity in HMIS, a
  household/person will be considered inactive and not reached out to until
  they reconnect with their case manager or service provider.
  • Clarification was provided regarding reinstation after 120 days. When a client
  is reinstated, they will go back to their “place in line” as matching looks at
  urgency of the client and not time on the list.
  • The Lived Experience Board reviewed the policy at the November meeting
  and agreed that the policy should be adopted but recommended extending
  the allowable “inactive” days from 90 to 120.
  • Discussion regarding the policy ensued.

  A motion was made by Co-Chair Shuford, seconded by Member Richert, to
  approve recommendation. The motion by the following vote:

  Yes:  13 Tan, Wee, Shuford, Martins, Pezzelle, Topolewski, Washington,
  Bambrick, Brezenoff, Weithers, Boyce, Richert, Chotiswatdi
  No:  0 None
  Recused: 0 None
  Abstain: 0 None
  Absent: 2 Wilson, Howat

4.  24-51719  Recommendation to receive and file the discussion on the 2024 CoC Board
  Retreat.

  Alexa Dixson-Griggs, CoC Program Coordinator presented.

  ⦁ The Board Retreat is upcoming and there are a few dates available. Staff have
  asked that the members have a quick look at their calendar to see if any if the dates
  will not fit in with their schedules.
  ⦁ A poll will be sent out to the Board later.

5.  24-51720  Recommendation to receive and file the Homeless Services Bureau Operations
  Report.

  Paul Duncan, Homeless Services Bureau Manager presented.
  ⦁ Catholic Charities has officially taken over the Family RRH Program from PATH
  as of 1/1/2024.
  ⦁ Lutheran Social Services is expecting to expand at the start of the new fiscal
  year once approval is granted.
  ⦁ The 2024 PIT Count will be on 1/25/2024 and more than 300 people have
  volunteered.
  ⦁ Homeless Services Bureau will begin on-site case management monitoring in
  February.
  ⦁ The LB CES has moved to an online system for HOP referrals, Coordinated
  Entry Verifications & Vacancy Notifications.
  ⦁ 60 Inclement weather beds at the MSC opened in December and are expected
  to be available through this winter season.
  ⦁ The MSC hosted a second pet vaccine day in partnership with Project Street
  Vet, a partnership that the MSC is looking to continue at least quarterly moving
  forward.
  ⦁ On MLK day, the MSC will hold a volunteer event to plant a community garden.
  ⦁ A second phone line counselor is up and answering calls at the MSC.
  ⦁ Encampment Resolution Fund, round 2 is staffing up, the goal is to launch initial
  sheltering efforts in early 2024. This includes entering a master lease using motel
  vouchers for interim shelter.
  ⦁ The city is working in partnership with LAHSA, Glendale and Pasadena CoC on
  the HHAP Round 5 application. The planned framework will be brought to the Board
  in March.
  ⦁ The Encampment Resolution Fund Round 3 application is being drafted, with
  the proposal to focus on state right aways and in partnership with state and county
  jurisdictions.
  ⦁ Construction for the Youth Center begins later this month, April Parker
  Foundation has been recommended to be the site operator.
  ⦁ A new request for proposals was released for the Project Homekey Best
  Western site.
  ⦁ Illumination Foundation has informed the City that they will not be renewing their
  contract at PHK Best Western. The city is to identify a new service provider in the
  interim. The goal is to make sure that those living at the site are not disrupted as
  much through the process.

6.  24-51721  Recommendation to receive and file the CoC Governance Report.

  Co-Chair Kimberly Wee provided an update on CoC Governance.
  ⦁ The next general meeting will be held via zoom, possible in person meetings in
  the future.

  Member Pam Chotiswatdi provided an update on HSAC.
  ⦁ The focus of HSAC within these last months has been on safe sleep sites.
  ⦁ HSAC Member are in conversation with the City Council members to advocate
  on behalf of a pilot program.
  ⦁ HSAC is also looking to increase Mayor’s Fund funding.

PUBLIC COMMENT

Ashley McKay from Impact Justice- Homecoming Project gave an introduction and brief overview of
the non-profit. She encourages the CoC Board to look into their services. They support those that
have been formerly incarcerated and connect them with those that have an empty room for housing.
100% of the participants have moved on to more permanent housing, and the program is thriving.

ANNOUNCEMENTS

ADJOURNMENT
